Lab 01 — DRIVER Target Selection

Category: Tuesday authenticated completion checkout, 25 or 0.

Mission

Learn DRIVER by completing one small, honest cycle: define a research-selection decision, represent a transparent screen, implement it with or without live data, validate one load-bearing claim, evolve the policy once, and reflect on a provisional public-company target. Technology readiness is the opening gate; the graded work is the finance workflow and decision.

Training sequence

  1. Readiness gate. Download Preflight Check and run the downloaded preflight_check.py locally or in Colab. If the primary path fails, preserve the exact symptom and download Offline Screening Case; use the downloaded offline-screening-case.csv. Name the owner and next action; never fabricate a successful download.
  2. Define & Discover — AI off. State the decision user, public-operating-company universe, exclusions, two measurable criteria, and one overriding disqualifier. Exclude banks, insurers, REITs, funds, shells, and other non-operating vehicles because the later Project 1 architecture is FCFF/enterprise-value based.
  3. Represent — human first. Write definitions, periods, thresholds or weights, missing-data treatment, and the smallest output needed to compare candidates.
  4. Implement the decision, not code — AI enabled. Use the published Week 1 dual-system packet, or send the same policy to two accessible course-supported systems. Author one follow-up probe and use a free interface when available; otherwise place COURSE-RUN PROBE: plus the exact probe and prediction in the AI-use checkout field. Mark one material suggestion accept, modify, reject, or unresolved, then apply your own policy to the live instructor diagnostics or the named offline case. Code implementation begins in Lab 02. No purchase is required and the access route never changes the scoring standard.
  5. Validate — AI may test; the human decides. AI may propose a test, but you independently check one load-bearing definition or company fact against provider documentation, a filing, or another authoritative source and decide whether the evidence is acceptable.
  6. Evolve — human-run in Lab 01; AI-assisted options begin in Lab 02. Test one alternative threshold, definition, or exclusion. Retain or revise the policy based on the result; do not manufacture a change.
  7. Reflect — human-owned. State what you now know, what remains unknown, and the observable evidence that would change your mind. Then select one provisional target for deeper valuation research.

This first cycle is a deliberate human-baseline calibration — a one-week teaching exception to DRIVER's normal 80%-AI middle, so you feel the manual cost the machine will absorb from Lab 02 on. Lab 02 is the first complete AI-accelerated middle: AI supports implementation, failure-hypothesis generation, and an Evolve robustness option; the student still owns the Define/Discover boundary, independent acceptance, and final Reflect decision.

The screen selects a research target. It does not establish a buy recommendation or intrinsic value. Asbury Automotive Group (ABG) is the instructor demonstration and is ineligible. Banks, insurers, REITs, funds, shells, and other non-operating vehicles are also ineligible for this Project 1 path.

Individual Brightspace checkout fields

  1. Lab Date (mm/dd/yyyy).
  2. Teammates and personal contribution (Purdue usernames; enter worked individually when applicable, then state what you personally defined, ran, checked, and decided).
  3. Readiness evidence: working path or exact blocker, fallback used, next action, and owner.
  4. Problem and decision: decision user, universe, research-selection purpose, and exclusions.
  5. Human baseline: two criteria with definitions and thresholds/weights plus one overriding disqualifier, written before generative AI.
  6. AI-use record: named access path; exact student-authored follow-up probe and prior prediction; returned or pending staff return status; and one material suggestion accepted, modified, rejected, or unresolved.
  7. Decision evidence: live source/provider and period/as-of date, or exact offline-case label; concise candidate comparison and provisional company/ticker.
  8. Validate, evolve, reflect: independent source/date/finding; alternative tested; retained or revised policy; what is known/unknown; and observable disqualifier/change condition.
  9. Optional artifact link if a durable repository/notebook exists.
  10. Truth and in-person attendance attestation: “I attended this session in person and completed this checkout only for myself. I produced and checked the evidence above, disclosed my AI use, and did not expose credentials.”
  11. Receipt confirmation: submit and open the Brightspace attempt/receipt before leaving.

Completion standard

Full credit requires an on-time authenticated attempt that directly answers every field, contains the requested personal work record, ends in a provisional target (or a defensible no admissible target yet result), and includes the attestation. Completing apply_student_screen() is not required until Lab 02. A reproducible technical failure can satisfy readiness evidence when the fallback finance task is completed; technology failure does not excuse or invalidate the finance decision work.
